symptoms: Small insects gather at the base of the plant near the water.
The plants start to dry up and look scorched.
You will see round patches in the field where plants are drying and falling over.
The insects suck the plant sap which stops grain from filling properly.
The plants may show signs of viral diseases like grassy stunt or ragged stunt.
photo_cues: Small curved eggs in leaf sheath
favourable_conditions: The pest thrives in humid conditions with continuous rice cultivation, high shade, and standing water in the field.
prevention: Do not plant the same susceptible rice variety in the same area every year.
Use resistant or tolerant rice varieties recommended for your state.
Avoid using too much nitrogen fertilizer.
Plant all fields in your area at the same time and keep the fields free of weeds.
Leave gaps of a few rows every 8 to 10 rows to help air move through the crop.
practices: Check your fields every 3 to 5 days by gently tapping the base of plants to see if insects jump into the water.
Drain the water from the field for 3 to 4 days if you see a heavy infestation.
Use light traps at night or yellow pan traps during the day to monitor and catch the insects.
Direct any sprays toward the base of the plants where the insects live.
Avoid using chemical pesticides if you see many natural enemies like spiders in the field.
